description: Tooltip glossary terms, role aliases, and mechanic definitions. Two sources: (1) roles reuse ability text from roles-40k.json; (2) mechanics are written here. EVERYTHING IS PUBLIC KNOWLEDGE — tooltips cannot leak hidden state.

roleGlossOverrides.heretic-priest: Wears the Priest's vestments and preaches the same sermons — but drift rises where it should fall. Finding one means noticing who got worse after a blessing.
roleGlossOverrides.murderer: The knife in the dark. Kills one player each night, and sits in the cabal's channel watching every other Heretic's plan.
roleGlossOverrides.sanctioned-psyker: One sanctioned warp-kill, once per game, against anyone. Firing it costs {driftWeight} drift — which lands the Psyker in Red, where a T2 scan executes them on sight. Nothing marks them: from the table they look exactly like a Murderer.
roleGlossOverrides.animus: Once per game, reaches for a player believed to be drowning in Red drift. If right, the Animus speaks in their name for a day and the body ruptures at dusk, revealing everything. If wrong, the attempt wastes in silence.

mechanics.label: Drift
mechanics.glossTemplate: The corruption the Warp leaves on a soul, scored 0 to {maxDrift}. It climbs when you act, kill, or vote with the losing side, and it never resets — you only ever feel it as a whisper, never as a number.

mechanics.label: The Warp
mechanics.gloss: The chaos dimension pressing against reality. Every forbidden gift in this game draws on it, and it always sends an invoice.

mechanics.label: Drift zone
mechanics.glossTemplate: Where a score sits on the ladder: Green ({greenMin}–{greenMax}), Yellow ({yellowMin}–{yellowMax}), Orange ({orangeMin}–{orangeMax}), Red ({redMin}–{redMax}), Black ({blackMin}). Powers read the zone, not the number.

mechanics.label: Torture
mechanics.gloss: The day vote's lesser verdict: the conclave breaks a suspect instead of killing them. Each round cripples the target one tier further and demands an answer. Not to be confused with the Interrogator, who works at night.

mechanics.label: Lynch
mechanics.glossTemplate: The day vote's fatal verdict. At {executionPercentage}% of the living — or against a suspect already marked — the conclave executes rather than tortures, and the body's allegiance is read out publicly.

mechanics.label: Crippled
mechanics.gloss: Torture damage. Tier 1 wounds, Tier 2 forces you to justify every vote aloud, Tier 3 shatters you. A crippled operative cannot take a night action.

mechanics.label: Confession
mechanics.gloss: What torture demands. The broken may confess, resist, or refuse and break — and at Tier 3 the conclave stops asking and simply demands it.

mechanics.label: Execute on Sight
mechanics.gloss: An Interrogator scan at T2 or higher against an Orange-or-worse target kills on the spot and reveals the alignment to everyone. It is why cheap nightly scans are worth the drift.

mechanics.label: Possession
mechanics.gloss: The Animus's one shot: reach into a player already in Red drift and speak with their voice for a day. When it ends the body ruptures and the Warp is visible to all.

mechanics.label: Blood Ritual
mechanics.gloss: A faction-wide Heretic move. Only one cabalite's claim lands each night, and it shares that Heretic's night action slot — taking it means giving up your own directive.

mechanics.label: Catalyst
mechanics.glossTemplate: The Recruiter's conversion. A player sitting at Black — drift {blackMin} — can be flipped to the Heretic side silently, and wakes already turned.

mechanics.label: The Conclave
mechanics.gloss: The assembled operatives — the table itself. It sits by day to accuse and vote, and disperses when the light withdraws.

mechanics.label: The Cabal
mechanics.gloss: The Heretics, collectively. They know one another from the first night, share a private channel, and win together.

mechanics.label: Heretic
mechanics.gloss: The Warp's servants, hidden among the faithful. They win by reaching parity with the Loyalists — by the knife, or by conversion.

mechanics.label: Loyalist
mechanics.gloss: The Emperor's faithful. They win by cutting the living Heretic count below parity, which means finding them before the nights run out.

mechanics.label: Parity
mechanics.gloss: The Heretic victory line: living Heretics equal or outnumber living Loyalists. Every night kill drags the table toward it.

mechanics.label: Sleep
mechanics.glossTemplate: Submitting no night action. It costs nothing and pays {sleepRecovery} drift, which is the only dependable way back down the ladder.
